title: Microsoft Teams

signIn.hint: Sign in with the demo account in the capture browser first; Teams opens on the last chat or channel.

rules.note: The app launcher's tooltip comes along when the pointer rested on it during a page capture (zoom captures). Pages only: in hover data it is the launcher's real tooltip.

raw: placeholder="Press ⌥ ⌘ G to go right to a chat or channel"
rules.note: Teams rotates the search box's hint between captures; one hint, so it doesn't change as the presenter zooms.

reflow.note: Teams lays itself out by script (chat list width, chip overflow, compact channel header), so each zoom level is the whole page captured at that zoom (record.zooms). The bands come from the recorded width and zoom (the engine's), never from fixed pixel widths: a demo writes { use: 'reflow' } and the recorder fills its bands.

channel-stick.note: The channel's posts stay scrolled to the newest one when the window gets shorter.

chat-list.note: The chat list: 280–400 px, applied on release, written as --slot-width in vw.

theme.setting: Settings and more › Settings › Appearance › Theme (Light, Dark, High contrast, Follow operating system theme)
fallbacks: Avatars and images keep their colors
High contrast: some Fluent v9 focus outlines and the app bar's selected pill differ

writes.what: Posts the message in the open chat or channel

undo.note: Teams keeps a "This message has been deleted" line; post only to the demo's own chat or a test channel.

check.expect: No post from the demo account after the run started, other than the demo's own.

writes.what: Changes the Teams theme (a setting that follows the account to every device)

check.expect: Theme reads what the demo starts with (Light unless it says otherwise).

effects.what: With Theme on "Follow operating system theme", Teams turns dark when the Mac or Windows is in dark mode

check.expect: The page renders light (its background's lightness above 0.6) with the OS in either mode.

notes: Fluent v9 tokens; Teams loads only the active theme's tokens, so the other themes come from themes/*.json (spike A). Hover cards show after 240–390 ms.

why./^POST login\\.microsoftonline\\.com\\/[: Entra's token endpoint: issues access tokens for the signed-in account; changes nothing in the tenant (Nov 23 review).
why./^POST teams\\.cloud\\.microsoft\\/ups\\: Reads people's presence (a list of users in, their status out); setting presence is another endpoint. Held, Teams shows 'status Unknown' (Nov 23).
why./^POST teams\\.cloud\\.microsoft\\/api\\: Reads display names for user ids. Held, a post's author shows as 'Unknown user' (Nov 23).
why./^POST teams\\.microsoft\\.com\\/api\\/a: Teams' auth service: turns the sign-in into a Teams session; held on a cold start, Teams stays on its sign-in splash (Nov 23).

filters.why: Teams draws its left rail's teams from its own store (IndexedDB), not from a response as it loads, so no response filter can leave a team out. Measured Nov 24: no response on load carried the team; Teams' conversations store did. Each team is a treeitem at aria-level 2 in the rail's tree, its channels in the group under it: a flow list, so a hidden team leaves no hole and the next moves up. Marked and hidden, never removed (React keeps its own nodes), and never in a snapshot.

ownStatus.why: Teams shows your own status on your avatar at the top right of every screen, and a replica keeps it. The capture browser's Teams never reports you active (Nov 25: four variants, no activity or presence call, all read Away), so your status comes from your own Teams app: away from your computer, it turns Away. Its name ends "for <account> in <organization>" in the Nov 19 recording, and at the status itself on Nov 25 ("Your profile, status Away").
ownStatus.name: /^Your profile, status (.+?)(?: for |$)/
